recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is recommended unless the work group later decides to narrow the mapping language itself rather than clarify the typical FHIR use case.
issue_request: FHIR-23007 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I change request asking the mapping-language page to reduce confusion caused by describing FHIR mapping instances as DAGs. The accepted resolution was to add a note that FHIR resources are strict hierarchies, i.e., trees.
initial_application: Commit 01e6c7f9a432144b5a8a7d4054feeacaad88284e applied FHIR-23007 by adding a note after the introductory DAG paragraph in source/mapping-language.html. Commit 0646c3096026cde98eca996d111806e36ed14572 then refined that note to the current wording: most contexts of use are strict mono-hierarchies (a.k.a trees), including FHIR specification types.
additional_context: The referenced Zulip thread confirms the concern was that readers might infer FHIR resources were not trees; Grahame clarified that FHIR resources are trees while the mapping language can work with broader DAG-shaped data, and agreed that a parenthetical note about typical FHIR tree-shaped use would resolve the confusion. source/hierarchy.xml lists mapping-language.html as the Mapping Language page, so the checked source file is in build scope. Jira searches for nearby DAG/tree mapping-language issues found only FHIR-23007, and Confluence searches found no conflicting minutes.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The combined branch already preserves the approved clarification directly after the DAG description, and replacing the remaining DAG wording would conflict with the accepted modification and Zulip clarification that the mapping language is broader than FHIR resource trees.

related_jiras.note: Same-day mapping-language commit refined the FHIR-23007 note wording while applying an unrelated source-statement clarification.
